items.answer: Water fills the vacuole, which pushes the cell contents and membrane hard against the cell wall. The cell is turgid and firm, so the plant stands. Without water the vacuole shrinks, the push fades, cells go flaccid and the plant wilts.
items.prompt: Explain why a plant stands up straight when it has plenty of water, and why it wilts without water.

items.answer: It means the membrane chooses what crosses it: some substances are let through while others are kept out.
